revisions.question: You have one completely free evening after a demanding week. Where are you most likely to invest it?

options.label: Make visible progress on one personally important result
Choose the most energizing or interesting possibility available
Give the time to a person or commitment that matters to me
Get absorbed in a subject, puzzle, or skill I want to understand more deeply

revisions.discriminator: Allocation of scarce discretionary energy toward impact, possibility, meaningful commitment, or absorbing understanding/mastery.
revisions.desirability_balance: Green is now a concrete, enjoyable evening choice rather than the person who evaluates the choices carefully. All four responses offer a legitimate form of restoration or satisfaction.

revisions.question: You are learning a subject for personal interest, with no test or deadline. What tells you it is time to move on?

options.label: I can use what I learned to accomplish the result I wanted
I have followed the most engaging questions and want a fresh direction
The interest feels meaningfully connected to something I value and has found a lasting place in my life
I can explain the core ideas and see how they fit together

revisions.discriminator: Completion through usable result, explored curiosity, personally meaningful continuity, or coherent understanding.
revisions.desirability_balance: Yellow no longer requires an external beneficiary. Its completion signal is personal meaning and continuity, alongside three equally legitimate completion standards.

revisions.question: Recognition feels more meaningful when it acknowledges the rigor and reliability behind my work than when it emphasizes the scale of the result.
revisions.discriminator: Recognition of rigor/reliability versus recognition of result scale.
revisions.desirability_balance: Both technical quality and visible scale are legitimate forms of recognition; the alternative no longer sounds superficial.

revisions.question: I am quicker to trust someone who takes ownership of moving a result forward than someone who builds trust through a steady, dependable process.
revisions.discriminator: Trust through owned forward movement versus trust through dependable process.
revisions.desirability_balance: Both people actively build trust through useful behavior; the alternative is no longer passive reassurance.

deferred_rationale.EXP2-S-18: The specialist-adviser scenario repeats the same result/possibility/continuity/evidence trust architecture already supplied by EXP1-S-05. Broadening purchase adviser to specialist does not add enough new measurement value for admission.

next_phase_recommendation: Further content expansion is not justified before assembler simulation. The 183-question research bank now has sufficient conceptual breadth to test selection frequency, within-attempt family collisions, format/color opportunities, context/tone distribution, and repeat exposure. Generate more content only if simulation identifies a specific measurable deficit.
